provenance.prompt:
J.120 / Piper Quickstep — DUNK-DOUBLE action sheet, attempt 1

Action canon: follow the explicit fifteen-pose two-pump sequence from `tools/generate-art/j103-keeg-dunk-double-prompt.md`, adapted to Piper's identity and style. This is a TWO-PUMP DUNK, not a single pump, windmill, reverse or 360 dunk.

Create one original production sprite sheet for Piper Quickstep performing a powerful two-pump basketball dunk for JAMVERSE '96. Canvas exactly 1536×1024 pixels, true transparent RGBA, five equal columns by three equal rows, strict row-major order, exactly fifteen distinct complete full-body drawings. Each cell is approximately 307×341 pixels. Keep every part of every pose—including the full high ponytail, every fingertip and both shoes—at least 28 pixels inside every cell edge. Preserve wide transparent gutters and outer margins, consistent scale, camera and anatomy. No pose may touch, cross, overlap or merge with a neighboring cell. No grid, borders, scenery, court, hoop, floor, shadow, effects, text, labels, teammate, opponent, ball, sphere, orb, prop or equipment.

Piper is the same athletic adult human woman in every pose: warm-brown skin, expressive dark-brown eyes and face, vivid bright-orange hair in a long high ponytail tied behind her head, natural adult athletic proportions, russet-red sleeveless basketball jersey and shorts with cream/white piping and paired cream side stripes, plain blank kit with no marks, red-and-cream high-top basketball shoes and white socks. Preserve her face, skin, hair shape/color, body proportions, uniform and shoes consistently. Exactly one head, two arms, two hands, two legs and two feet, natural joints and five fingers on each visible hand. No costume changes, jewelry, numbers, text, logo, extra limbs, missing limbs or altered anatomy. Match the detailed JAMVERSE Piper artwork and established sprite-sheet style; do not switch to pixelated rendering.

Both hands stay empty: the basketball is separate game art and must never appear in the drawings. Before the sole release, Piper's hands mime the invisible ball. Pose10 (zero-based; fifth column, second row) is the one release at simulation tick21 on the SECOND pump: arm fully extended toward the rim, palm open and empty. Poses0–9 retain the ball; poses11–14 are empty-handed follow-through, descent, landing and recovery. The two pump peaks must be visually and mechanically distinct: first overhead pump at pose5, then clearly lower reset to chest at pose6, then second, higher pump across poses7–10. Do not make a single continuous reach.

Keep Piper facing and approaching image-right. Distinct connected keyframes, strict row-major:
0. Right-facing approach with hands low.
1. Gather the invisible ball near the waist.
2. Two-foot plant and crouch.
3. Takeoff, ball-miming hand rises to the chest.
4. First pump: hand lifts toward the shoulder.
5. First overhead pump: hand reaches above the crown, ponytail and face unobstructed.
6. Clearly lowers and resets the invisible ball at the chest after the first pump.
7. Second drive begins, torso tightens and knees tuck.
8. Second pump raises the hand higher than the first overhead peak.
9. Full second-pump extension toward the rim, still holding the invisible ball.
10. Sole release at tick21: fully extended straight shooting arm, open empty palm.
11. Empty-handed follow-through through the imagined rim plane.
12. Descent with legs tucked.
13. Controlled two-foot landing, knees flexed.
14. Stable recovery, both hands empty.

Make all fifteen poses visibly distinct, anatomically complete and mechanically connected. Keep both hands empty and never draw the ball. Check each pose for cell separation, full anatomy, Piper identity, clean transparency and at least28px margins. Use no backdrop, matte, glow, haze, alpha fringe, speckles, repeated/merged bodies or extra art. Favor pose clarity over figure size. Return only the sprite sheet.
